title: Improving the Reconstruction of Disentangled Representation Learners via Multi-Stage Modeling
summary: Splits disentangled representation learning into two stages, a penalty-based model that infers independent factors and a second conditional model that recovers the correlated residual, so reconstruction quality is regained without weakening disentanglement, and shows the construction can be realised with variational autoencoders, adversarial networks or normalising flows. A closing section carries the method to simulated credit tabular data, where TVAE is one of two benchmark generators trained against it and its mode-specific normalization is set out as the reference treatment of mixed continuous and discrete columns.
evidence: section 6.1, headed Baseline models, describes the TVAE framework of Xu et al. (2019), its one-hot encoding of discrete columns and its mode-specific normalization of continuous columns by Gaussian mixture, each variable becoming a pair giving the chosen mode and the value normalized within it; section 6.4 and Table 1 report Jensen-Shannon divergence and correlation-distance scores for MS-VAE against TVAE and beta-TCVAE at latent dimension 9, and Figures 7 and 8 compare per-column distributions, noting TVAE misses an underrepresented category. The paper's own preprocessing is log transform plus min-max normalization, so the TVAE encoding is described rather than adopted

title: Causal-TGAN: Generating Tabular Data Using Causal Generative Adversarial Networks
summary: Introduces Causal-TGAN, a tabular generator that conditions generation on a causal graph over the columns so that samples follow the causal structure rather than the joint distribution alone, and reports performance close to the strongest baseline while requiring only a partial graph. CTGAN is the leading comparison generator, its Gaussian-mixture encoding of continuous columns is adopted for every model in the study, and all reported metrics are computed with the SDV package's single-table evaluation module.
evidence: section 4.1 states that implementations provided by the SDV package are used for all the metrics above, footnote 3 pointing to sdv.dev/SDV/user_guides/evaluation/single_table; section 4.2 compares Causal-TGAN against PrivBN, MedGAN, TableGAN and CTGAN at 300 epochs and batch size 500, states that the variables are encoded by the method proposed in Xu et al. (2019) with a Gaussian mixture model for continuous columns, and reports in Tables 2 and 3 that CTGAN ties for best average column similarity and is best on machine-learning efficacy for adult and news. Recorded api_user rather than baseline_only because running an SDV-family tool outranks the comparison role, following the DP-CGANS precedent

title: Improving Model Compatibility of Generative Adversarial Networks by Boundary Calibration
summary: Adds a boundary-calibration loss to adversarial training that penalises generated points falling across decision boundaries approximated by classifiers pretrained on the real data, and reports that the resulting BWGAN and BMMDGAN raise the accuracy of models trained on synthetic data across four UCI tables and two image sets without losing sample quality. CTGAN supplies the machine-learning-efficacy criterion the paper adopts as its measure of model compatibility and is the tabular prior work it positions against, but it is not run.
evidence: the introduction names the target property model compatibility [24] or machine learning efficacy [32], where reference [32] is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni, Modeling tabular data using conditional GAN, NeurIPS 2019, and credits [32] as the pioneering work showing conditional GANs give better model compatibility than VAEs; section 3 contrasts the proposed loss with Tabular GAN [32] and states the method applies to most GAN variants including it; the compared methods in section 5.1 are WGAN, MMD GAN and ACGAN with their BC-loss counterparts, and Tables 1 to 5 carry no CTGAN row

title: Adversarial random forests for density estimation and generative modeling
summary: Proposes adversarial random forests, which alternate between fitting a forest to discriminate real from synthetic data and resampling until the two are indistinguishable, yielding a density estimator (FORDE) and a generator (FORGE) that match deep tabular models on accuracy at a small fraction of their training cost. The real-data evaluation is Xu et al.'s tabular benchmark reproduced in full, with CTGAN and TVAE run from the SDV API implementations as two of the five deep baselines.
evidence: section 5 states the real-data evaluation recreates a benchmarking pipeline originally proposed by Xu et al. (2019) and introduces CTGAN and TVAE as the conditional tabular GAN and tabular VAE that pipeline was built around; appendix B.3 reproduces the workflow step by step from the same datasets, adult, census, credit, covertype, intrusion, mnist12 and mnist28; footnotes 6 and 7 name sdv.dev/SDV/api_reference/tabular/ctgan.html and the matching tvae.html as the implementations used; Table 2 reports accuracy, F1 and runtime for CTGAN and TVAE against FORGE, Table 5 repeats the comparison on the MNIST subsets, and section 5 records FORGE completing the pipeline about 85 times faster than CTGAN and 35 times faster than TVAE
needs: importance 4 against 3 rests on a convention that does not exist yet. The paper does not extend CTGAN's conditional vector or mode-specific normalization, which is the current test for lifting baseline_only to 4, but its entire real-data evaluation is Xu et al.'s benchmark reproduced datasets and all, run on the SDV implementations. Recorded 4; drop to 3 if adopting the benchmark wholesale does not qualify

title: Subpopulation-Specific Synthetic EHR for Better Mortality Prediction
summary: Identifies the subpopulations on which a mortality-prediction model underperforms, generates synthetic records for each of them separately, and trains a per-subpopulation ensemble on the augmented data, reporting gains over both a real-data-only ensemble and SMOTE on two MIMIC use cases. CTGAN is the generator throughout: one model is trained per underrepresented subpopulation on training-set samples only and then sampled to add between 0 and 1000 percent of that subpopulation's real size.
evidence: the related-work section states that Xu et al. proposed the Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN), which is used in this research; section 3.1 step 2 trains a CTGAN on each underrepresented subpopulation until convergence on an RTX6000, with discriminator and generator learning rates, discriminator steps, epochs and batch size given in Table 1, and step 3 samples 0 to 1000 percent of the subpopulation size; Table 2 reports ROCAUC at the best augmentation level against a real-only per-subpopulation ensemble and against SMOTE, and the discussion describes the work as applying CTGAN together with an ensemble-like approach

title: TabEBM: A Tabular Data Augmentation Method with Distinct Class-Specific Energy-Based Models
summary: Fits a separate energy-based model per class, using a pretrained in-context classifier as the surrogate so no generator training is needed, and argues that estimating each class distribution on its own avoids the degradation joint-distribution generators show on very small tables; augmentation then improves downstream accuracy where the compared generators reduce it. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the eight benchmark generators, run at default settings from their Synthcity implementations across accuracy, fidelity and privacy comparisons.
evidence: section 4 lists eight generators of eight categories and names TVAE as the variational autoencoder method and CTGAN as the generative adversarial method, both cited to reference [85], Xu et al.; appendix B.6 states that the six remaining benchmark generators use their open-source implementations in Synthcity at default settings, so the SDV-family models are run through that wrapper rather than from sdv-dev; Table 1 reports balanced accuracy for CTGAN and TVAE against TabEBM at 20, 50, 100 and 200 real samples, and Figures 4, 5 and 7 add the class-imbalance, fidelity and distance-to-closest-record comparisons

title: NRGBoost: Energy-Based Generative Boosted Trees
summary: Trains gradient-boosted trees to maximise a local second-order approximation of the likelihood rather than a loss against a supervised target, giving an energy-based generative model that supports single-variable inference at the level of a discriminative boosted-tree model while sampling by Gibbs. TVAE is one of the compared generators, taken from the SDV package and tuned over fifty trials of random search.
evidence: appendix D.3.7 states that the implementation of TVAE is taken from the SDV package, footnoted to github.com/sdv-dev/SDV, and tuned with 50 trials of random search over the space in Table 8; section 5 introduces TVAE (Xu et al., 2019) alongside TabDDPM and Forest-Flow as the compared deep and tree-based generators on top of the ARF and DEF baselines, and the machine-learning-efficacy and discriminator-measure tables report TVAE against NRGBoost on all seven datasets, with Figures 3 and 4 showing its California Housing and MNIST samples
